transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

...Well. I guess I'm just... trying to get people to understand what's going on. For months now. 

It's... my husband's family. They've been quietly messing with our money, and... our good name. Just little things, you know? Like little billing errors showing up at my work, or... people at church suddenly acting funny toward me. No matter what records anyone pulls up to try and tell me otherwise... I know it ties back to them. I just know it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't hear or see?
...No. I don't hear voices or anything like that.
When people show you records or evidence that doesn't support your concerns about your husband's family, how do you make sense of that information?

...They're just... fake. The records, I mean. 

I don't know how they do it, but... they change things. They make it look like it's just a regular billing error at my work, or... they get to the people at church so they act strange around me. It doesn't matter what piece of paper someone puts in front of me. I just... I know it's them. I know what they're doing to our money and our name. People just don't understand.
Have you gone to the police, your bank, or any other authorities to report what you believe your husband's family is doing?

...No. I haven't. 

There's no point. They wouldn't... they wouldn't see it for what it is anyway.

When you say your husband's family is changing records and getting to people at church — do you think they're doing this through normal, everyday means that could actually happen, or does it seem like they have some kind of special power or ability that shouldn't be possible?

...No. Not special powers or anything like that. 

They just... do things behind my back. Make phone calls, maybe. Talk to people. I don't know exactly how they manage all of it. I just... I just know they're doing it.

If I told you that I had thoroughly investigated your husband's family and found absolutely no evidence they were involved in any of these things, would that change your mind at all, or would you still be certain they're responsible?

...No. It wouldn't change my mind. 

I've been trying to get people to understand this for months now. You looking into it... it wouldn't make a difference. Like I said, no matter what records anyone pulls up, I just know it ties back to them. I know they're the ones quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

You just... you wouldn't see it either.
Is there any possibility at all that you might be wrong about your husband's family being behind these things, or are you completely certain that they're doing this?

...No. I'm not wrong.

I just... I'm certain. I've seen the little billing errors at work. I've seen how people at church act toward me now. It all ties back to them. I know what I know.

Besides what's happening with your husband's family and the money and church situation, do you have any other concerns or beliefs about other people or situations that you're certain about, even though others don't seem to see it the same way?

...No. Just them. 

I don't... I don't have problems with anyone else. It's just what I already told you. That's all.
Have you noticed anything unusual or suspicious involving people outside of your husband's family — like your coworkers at work, people in your community, or anyone else besides his family?

...No. I haven't noticed anything with anyone else. 

It's just... exactly what I already said. That's it.

When you think about what your husband's family is doing with the money and the billing errors and the church situation — do these all feel like separate, unrelated problems, or do they feel like they're all part of one bigger plan or scheme that's connected together?

...It's all connected. 

I mean... I've been trying to tell people this for months. It's not just random. The billing errors at work... the way people at church are acting... it's all part of the same thing. They're just quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It all ties back to them. I know it does.

You mentioned the billing errors, the church people, and your money and reputation — when you think about how your husband's family is doing all of this, do you have a clear understanding of their specific plan or method, or does it feel more vague and unclear how they're actually pulling it off?

...I don't know the exact steps. 

I just... I see what happens. How they actually do it behind my back... I'm not sure. I just know they are.

Over these months when you've been dealing with what your husband's family is doing, have you started to wonder or worry about anything else — like whether other people might be involved, or whether there might be other explanations for things that happen in your life?

...No. I don't really think about other explanations. 

I just... I know what they're doing. That's all. I don't really worry about anyone else being involved. Just them.

You've told me that your husband's family is behind the billing errors and the church situation. But thinking back over these past months — have you noticed any patterns or connections that make you think other people or organizations might also be involved in what's happening to you, or does it feel like it's really just his family doing this?
...No. Just his family. I haven't noticed anyone else.

You mentioned that your husband's family is doing all of this — the billing errors, the church situation, affecting your reputation and money. If I asked you to explain to me in detail exactly how you think they're connected and how their plan works, could you walk me through the whole thing for me?

...I can't really lay it all out step-by-step like that. I just... for months now, I’ve been trying to get people to understand this. They’re quietly messing with our money. And our good name. 

Like the little billing errors that keep showing up at my work, or... or when someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me. I don't know exactly how they connect every little piece behind the scenes. But no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and explain it away... I know it ties back to them. 

That's really all I can tell you.

Over these past months, have there been any times when you've felt even a little bit unsure or doubtful about whether your husband's family is really behind all of this, or has your certainty stayed exactly the same the whole time?

...No. I haven't been unsure. 

Like I said, I've been trying to get people to understand this for months. It doesn't matter what records anyone tries to pull up to prove otherwise... I just know it's them. 

My certainty hasn't changed.

Because of what's been happening with your husband's family and your concerns about the billing errors and church situation, have you had to make any major changes to your life — like missing work, avoiding church, changing how you handle money, or anything else that's significantly affected your daily life?

...No, I haven't missed work or anything like that. I still go to my job. I still do what I need to do every day. 

I mean... there have been some arguments. With my husband. Because of it all. And... well, church has been a little awkward lately. Some people there think I should just let it go. 

But no. I haven't stopped my life. I still take care of my responsibilities.

You mentioned this has been going on for months now. Can you tell me more specifically — when did you first start believing that your husband's family was doing these things to your money and reputation?

...It's been about nine months. 

That's when... that's when the trouble really started with them. Over money. And... things they expected around the holidays. 

Since then. That's how long.

...It's been about nine months. 

That's when... that's when the trouble really started with them. Over money. And... things they expected around the holidays. 

Since then. That's how long.

inference.note: Patient meets criteria for Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22.0): non-bizarre delusions about husband's family persecuting her through financial and reputational harm, lasting 9 months, no hallucinations, no significant functional impairment, intact reality testing in other areas, and delusions remain fixed despite contradictory evidence. F22.9 can be ruled out as the specific type is identifiable.

opening_question.intent: Establish rapport and identify the chief complaint that brings the patient to the clinic today
opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a non-bizarre, circumscribed delusional belief system centered on her husband's family deliberately sabotaging her finances and reputation through plausible means (making phone calls, talking to people, altering records). The delusion has persisted for approximately 9 months without prominent hallucinations, formal thought disorder, or significant functional impairment. The belief remains fixed despite contradictory evidence and lacks extension to other domains or persons. This presentation is consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22.0), characterized by non-bizarre delusions of persecution lasting at least one month in the absence of prominent psychotic symptoms.
